intro.title: Simple Todo List
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple todo list application where you can add, view, and remove tasks. You will learn how to manage a list of items using Vue's reactive state and handle user interactions with event handlers. The main technologies involved are Vue components, the `ref` function for state, and event binding with `v-on` or `@`. This project will help you understand the basics of dynamic data and user input in Vue.
intro.usecase: Todo lists are foundational UI patterns that appear in countless real-world applications beyond simple task managers. Developers implement similar list management interfaces for e-commerce shopping carts, project management dashboards (like Trello cards), and content moderation queues where items can be added, marked complete, or removed. Understanding this pattern is essential for building interactive features like notification centers, user preference checklists, or admin panels where dynamic item management is required. Mastering todo list implementation provides the core skills for handling user-generated lists in applications ranging from personal productivity tools to enterprise software.

objectives: Initialize and manage a reactive todo list array using Vue's ref or reactive API
Implement a form handler to capture user input and add new todo items to the list
Bind form inputs to reactive data properties using v-model for two-way data binding
Render dynamic lists of todo items using v-for directives with proper key attributes
Configure click handlers to toggle todo completion status using Vue event binding
Manipulate the todo list array by implementing a function to remove completed items
Integrate conditional rendering with v-if or v-show to display completion feedback
Construct a complete Vue component that combines reactive state, event handlers, and template rendering

steps.seedCode:
<script>
import { ref } from 'vue';

// Create the SimpleTodoList component here
export default {
  setup() {
    // Initialize todos state with ref here
    const todos = ref([]);
    
    // Initialize newTodo state with ref here
    const newTodo = ref('');
    
    // Define addTodo handler function here
    function addTodo() {
      if (newTodo.value.trim()) {
        todos.value.push({ id: Date.now(), text: newTodo.value });
        newTodo.value = '';
      }
    }
    
    // Define removeTodo handler function here
    function removeTodo(id) {
      todos.value = todos.value.filter(todo => todo.id !== id);
    }
    
    // Return todos, newTodo, addTodo, and removeTodo from setup
    return {
      todos,
      newTodo,
      addTodo,
      removeTodo
    };
  }
};
</script>

<template>
  <!-- Todo list will go here -->
  <input v-model="newTodo" placeholder="Add a new todo">
  <!-- Add button here -->
</template>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Add' appears next to the input field. Clicking it will trigger the addTodo function to add the current input value to the todos list.
successCriteria: A <button> element with @click="addTodo" is added after the input field.
